children: Nokia, Nscale and other founding partners have formed a European consortium to develop artificial-intelligence infrastructure across the Nordics and Baltics.

The AI Gigafactory Northern consortium will connect AI infrastructure across a multisite network of AI gigafactories--large-scale facilities dedicated to developing and training next-generation AI models--located in Finland, Estonia, Latvia and Sweden.
Founding members include Nokia, Nscale, Skeleton, Telia and Verda.

"The sites will combine large-scale AI computing infrastructure with sovereign cloud and AI platform services, high-capacity connectivity and decarbonised energy," the consortium partners said in a joint statement.

Distributing capacity across several locations will allow the consortium to draw on multiple sources of energy, expand computing infrastructure where capacity is available and reduce reliance on any single site or supplier. The consortium said that would strengthen operational resilience and support cross-border expansion as European demand for AI grows.

The move comes after the European Union earlier this year launched a bidding process for large-scale AI gigafactories in an effort to build out the bloc's own tech capabilities and catch up with rivals like the U.S.

Through an initiative known as InvestAI, the EU aims to mobilize 30 billion euros, equivalent to $33.1 billion, for AI investment, combining 20 billion euros of private-sector funding with 10 billion euros from EU and member state public funding.
